title: Agent Certificate v0 Common Types
description: Shared bounded semantic types for the Agent Certificate v0 contract family (Wave-C C6/C1 reconciled rulings, 2026-08-11). Design rules this family encodes: (1) no user-controlled free text is reachable from any certificate or registry record — every string is const, enum, or pattern-anchored; (2) cryptographic material crosses only through NAMED semantic types defined here (per C1 Ruling 1: 'Permit fixed-size cryptographic material only through named semantic types … do not pretend these types are content-free' — each such type is a disclosed information channel and carries a Disclosure Register audience note in its description); (3) tier 4 is present in the ClaimTier enum but structurally unconstructible in any v0 claim (C6 Ruling 5: 'Keep tier 4 in the schema, but make v0 emission of it a compile error'). This is a definitions-only document; it has no root instance shape.

Sha256Digest.description: Named semantic type: a lowercase-hex SHA-256 commitment digest with explicit scheme prefix (same surface rule as optimization/best_config_hash_contract_schema.json#/definitions/sha256_digest). NOT content-free: a digest over an enumerable preimage is guessable unless the commitment used secret blinding (C1 Ruling 4: 'commitments over enumerable preimages require secret blinding, not public salt'). Every field of this type is an issuer->relying-party or client->server disclosure and must have a Disclosure Register entry before a new use site ships.

OpaqueRef.description: Named semantic type: a namespaced opaque reference token (server- or issuer-assigned; never client free text). The namespace prefix is a closed lowercase token; the identifier body is bounded base64url-safe material. An OpaqueRef is a stable identifier and therefore a linkability channel, not content-free (C1 tension T3): raw public keys are NOT represented — key references cross only as OpaqueRef.

ClientKeyRefV0.description: Named semantic type: a project-scoped client verification-key reference. It is derived, never caller-selected: `ckr:` plus base64url-without-padding of SHA-256(UTF8(traigent.agent_certificate.client_key_ref.v0) || uint64be(len(project_ref)) || UTF8(project_ref) || uint64be(len(signature_algorithm)) || UTF8(signature_algorithm) || uint64be(len(canonical SubjectPublicKeyInfo DER)) || canonical SubjectPublicKeyInfo DER). The 32-byte digest is rendered as exactly 43 base64url characters. This pseudonymous client verification-key identifier is a disclosed linkability channel; it carries no private key or evidence content.

ProjectRefV0.description: Bounded project identity used as the public scope input to the derived ClientKeyRefV0. This is control-plane identity only and never contains agent, evaluator, dataset, or build-process content.

GitCommitSha.description: Named semantic type: a full 40-hex git commit SHA pinning an implementation ref (used by the D2 payload to pin the SDK witness ref; C1 Ruling 4: the e97b030f strace witness 'does not automatically cover newly added certificate code. It must be rerun at the new pinned implementation ref').

BoundedSemver.description: Named semantic type: a bounded semantic-version token (no pre-release/build free text — those would be an uncontrolled string channel).

SignatureBytes.description: Named semantic type: canonical RFC 4648 base64 of exactly 64 raw signature bytes (86 base64 data characters followed by `==`). Ed25519 uses its 64-byte raw encoding; ECDSA P-256 uses fixed IEEE-P1363 `r || s`, 32 bytes each. The verifier MUST enforce low-S for ECDSA before accepting the raw signature. NOT content-free — signature bytes are cryptographic material with their own Disclosure Register entry (C1 Ruling 5, client->server entry 3 / issuer->relying-party section).

PublicNonce.description: Named semantic type: a bounded lowercase-hex public nonce. Register entry 8 wording is BINDING and travels with every use site: a public salt or nonce 'does not prevent dictionary guessing' (C1 Ruling 5, entry 8; Ruling 4: guessing resistance requires secret blinding, a keyed commitment, or a deliberately expensive construction).

ClaimTier.description: The full four-tier claim scale, present in the schema as owner-resolved (C6 Ruling 5: removing tier 4 'violates the tiered owner resolution'). 1 = client-attested; 2 = server-record-backed (HMAC trust boundary; not externally verifiable); 3 = asymmetrically issuer-signed; 4 = client-co-signed, gap-checked. Tier semantics are pinned by the signed semantics manifest. Tier is a property of each CLAIM, never of a certificate ('is this certificate tier 3?' is a malformed question). v0 claim instances MUST use EmittableClaimTierV0, which keeps tier 4 in this enum while making its emission unconstructible.

EmittableClaimTierV0.description: The v0 emission constraint (C6 Ruling 5, reconciled): 'Keep tier 4 in the schema, but make v0 emission of it a compile error.' Tier 4 remains a member of the ClaimTier enum above; this type conjoins that enum with a structural exclusion, so NO valid v0 claim instance can carry tier 4 — a tier-4 claim is schema-invalid, i.e. a compile error, not a runtime policy. Enabling tier 4 is a MAJOR version event with fresh verifier evidence (C1 Ruling 1: 'Tier 4 is rejected in v0. Enabling it requires a major version and fresh verifier evidence'; 'Enabling a previously impossible tier changes accepted semantics').

CommitmentSchemeV0.description: Closed commitment-scheme vocabulary. For sha256_secret_blinded_v1, each slot_commitment_digest MUST be `sha256:` followed by lowercase hexadecimal HMAC-SHA-256, with key=blind and data=UTF8("traigent.cert.v0.slot_commitment.v1") || 0x00 || UTF8(artifact_kind) || 0x00 || jcs_v1(artifact_document). The domain tag is fixed, artifact_kind is one of the four fixed slot enum values, and artifact_document is a client-local JSON object accepted only by jcs_v1 (no floats). Blind is exactly 32 cryptographically random bytes, independently generated per slot per build, client-local, never transmitted, logged, or reused; opening and recomputation are client-local operations. (C1 Ruling 4 binding rule: 'commitments over enumerable preimages require secret blinding, not public salt'.) A public-salt scheme is deliberately NOT registered; per the same ruling there is 'none for public-salt guessing' as a reversal condition.

CanonicalizationProfileV0.description: Closed canonicalization-profile vocabulary for commitment preimages. jcs_v1 = RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme, floats banned from preimages (C1 Ruling 4: 'Banning floats is sensible for canonicalization' — the float64 covert-channel arithmetic was struck, the canonicalization ban stands). PINNED REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION (SCHEMA-1, 2026-08-24, gap C6: 'the declared JCS is not implemented'): traigent_schema/fp2.py (normative document docs/fingerprints/fp2.md, packaged conformance corpus traigent_schema/data/fp2_conformance.json) fixes RFC 8785 number formatting via the ECMAScript Number::toString algorithm and orders object keys by UTF-16 code unit rather than code point — the two rules RFC 8785 needs and Python's own json.dumps(sort_keys=True) does not provide, which is exactly the divergence gap C6 identified. Every unsigned-manifest digest (certificate_unsigned_manifest_v0_schema.json#/definitions/UnsignedManifestV0) and every client-local commitment digest (certificate_client_evidence_manifest_v0_schema.json) MUST be computed with this implementation (or an implementation proven byte-identical against traigent_schema/data/fp2_conformance.json); every value entering a jcs_v1 preimage MUST already satisfy fp2's own rejection rules (no float, no non-finite number, no unsafe integer, no lone surrogate) in addition to this contract family's float ban.

SignatureAlgorithmV0.description: Closed signature-algorithm vocabulary for the v0 issuer and co-attestation paths. The v0 issuer path is a NEW dedicated per-environment certificate-signing key through protected GitHub-OIDC CI (C6 Ruling 4); this vocabulary deliberately does NOT reuse ArtifactSignatureEnvelopeV2 — 'Adding nested signatures and new fields changes the format and verifier' (C6 Ruling 3(iv), struck reuse).

BuildSessionSubjectV0.description: The machine-readable build_session subject (conceded to the proposer: 'the mandatory page-one scope box and machine-readable build_session subject'). The certificate is ABOUT a build session and nothing else. MOVED HERE (SCHEMA-1, 2026-08-24 pre-issuance correction) from agent_certificate_v0_schema.json so both the printed certificate's `subject` field and the signed unsigned-manifest's `subject` coverage section (certificate_unsigned_manifest_v0_schema.json#/definitions/UnsignedManifestV0) reference the identical type — a compiler that copies the same object into both places, verified structurally identical rather than merely described as such (closes gap C1: 'coverage is a label, not a binding'). This REUSES the orphaned optimization/certificate_subject_schema.json subject-binding SHAPE — a self-describing hash_algorithm carried outside the hashed content, a commitment digest, and exact envelope-version pinning, with that schema's own scope discipline ('It does not certify provenance') restated here for the build session. The full certificate_subject RECORD is deliberately NOT embedded: its config_id is a caller-chosen string (bounded at 128 chars but otherwise free), and embedding it would open a user-controlled free-text channel into a certificate record, which the boundary rule forbids ('certificate and registry records contain no user-controlled free-text fields'). SCOPE, stated so it is not over-read: this subject identifies WHICH build session the certificate concerns. It does not certify the session's provenance, contents, or completeness.

hash_algorithm.description: The algorithm under which session_commitment_digest was computed — reused from the certificate-subject shape's single normative definition so a subject can never be compared across algorithms; an unknown value fails closed. The pinned enum is `v1`, NOT `sha256` (C0: the pre-correction compiler defaulted to the wrong value and thereby produced a schema-invalid document — see test_hash_algorithm_rejects_sha256_default).

build_session_ref.description: Opaque build-session reference; MUST match ledger_seal_projection.build_session_ref and, inside the signed unsigned manifest, seal.build_session_ref (compiler-checked equality; cross-field equality is not expressible in draft-07 across $ref boundaries).

session_commitment_digest.description: Canonical commitment digest binding the subject to the sealed session content.

DataFlowModeV0.description: Closed data-flow-mode vocabulary, grounded in the two modes already named elsewhere in this contract family: 'offline' (the retained future D2 payload shape, C6 Ruling 5) and 'current_online' (mandatory non-claim NC_CURRENT_ONLINE_FREETEXT: 'Current-online mode discloses tuned free-text configuration values'). No third mode is added here — inventing one would be a policy selection between competing registers this packet is not authorized to make (SCHEMA-1 stop condition). Used by the unsigned manifest's privacy_mode coverage section as the session-level declaration; D2 is unsupported in frozen v0.

SdkIdentityV0.description: The build session's SDK identity: the pinned implementation ref plus its release version. Grounded in the retained future D2 payload's sdk_ref parameter (C1 Ruling 4), generalized to a session-level coverage section so the signed manifest binds SDK identity; D2 is unsupported in frozen v0.

CompilerRegisterVersionsV0.description: The build session's compiler and pinned-register identities: the compiler build that will emit the certificate plus the five digests SemanticsBindingV0 already prints on the certificate face (agent_certificate_v0_schema.json#/definitions/SemanticsBindingV0). This is a SEPARATE, structurally independent definition rather than a $ref to SemanticsBindingV0 — referencing it would make certification_common_v0_schema.json depend on agent_certificate_v0_schema.json, which already depends on certification_common_v0_schema.json (for BuildSessionSubjectV0), a file cycle. Compiler-checked equality obligation instead: this section's five digest fields MUST equal certificate.semantics's five fields exactly, and compiler_version MUST equal any printed C1 claim's params.compiler_version. Draft-07 cannot check either equality once only the manifest_digest crosses.

SignedMaterialDomainTagV0.description: Closed domain-separator vocabulary for the two v0 signature roles. Domain separation prevents material for one role being accepted for another. The issuer projection excludes the outer client co_attestation: issuer material = UTF8(`traigent.agent_certificate.issuer_signature.v0`) || uint64be(len(manifest_jcs_bytes)) || manifest_jcs_bytes. The client projection includes issuer_signature and excludes only its own outer co_attestation: client material = UTF8(`traigent.agent_certificate.client_co_attestation.v0`) || uint64be(len(certificate_projection_jcs_bytes)) || certificate_projection_jcs_bytes. Neither preimage contains the other role's raw signature bytes. The tag is a fixed property of the signing role, not a wire field of the signature record. Signature bytes are computed from, never included in, the signed documents, so no digest fixed point exists.

DigestRoleDomainTagV0.description: Closed role-domain vocabulary for load-bearing certificate digests. Each digest is `sha256:` plus lowercase SHA-256 over UTF8(role_domain_v1) || 0x00 || jcs_v1(document). Distinct role tags MUST be used for unsigned manifests, pre-issuance audit reports, claim-material projections, the issuer-signed client certificate projection, and the client-local evidence-manifest root; the slot HMAC commitment formula is separate and unchanged.
